items.title: Campbell’s Cuts 13% of Workforce in Effort to Turn Around Struggling Operations
items.summary: Campbell’s has announced a significant workforce reduction, cutting 13% of its employees (over 1,750 jobs), as part of a cost-saving initiative aimed at revitalizing its struggling operations. This decision follows a quarterly loss driven by increased costs and soft consumer demand, trends that the company anticipates will continue. The company plans to achieve $500 million in cost reductions by fiscal year 2030.

items.title: We believe inflation is likely to surprise to the downside, says Morgan Stanley's Matthew Hornbach
items.summary: Matthew Hornbach, Morgan Stanley global head of macro strategy, believes that inflation is likely to surprise to the downside. He joined 'Squawk Box' to discuss the economy's condition, the Federal Reserve's battle against inflation, the effects of tariffs, and the future path of interest rates. The discussion also covered various economic and policy topics.

items.title: Broadcom Stock Falls Afterhours Despite Strong Earnings Report
items.summary: Broadcom's shares declined by about 3.4% in after-hours trading despite the company reporting strong third-quarter results. The chipmaker exceeded analyst expectations for revenue, reaching $29.6 billion, an 86% increase year-over-year. However, the results, while positive, did not significantly surpass already high investor expectations, leading to the stock's dip.

items.title: StealthGas Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
items.summary: StealthGas reported strong Q2 2026 earnings with a net income of $17.3 million and EPS of $0.46, despite lower revenue due to a reduced fleet. The company achieved a debt-free balance sheet with over $250 million in liquidity, primarily from an insurance settlement and asset sales, and plans to use this capital for fleet renewal while continuing to divest older vessels. Geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East have increased ton-miles and supported shipping rates, particularly for larger vessels, but also led to decreased LPG imports in India and China, creating market uncertainties.

items.title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Falls 5% as Supply Constraints Overshadow Raised Guidance, Super Micro Slips, Dell Holds Steady
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) stock dropped 5% despite strong Q3 results and raised guidance, primarily due to supply constraints limiting its ability to fulfill orders for memory, CPUs, and drives. While Dell and Super Micro Computer also navigate the high demand for AI infrastructure, HPE's long-term outlook remains positive with an Oracle networking deal and ambitious fiscal 2027 targets for revenue, EPS, and free cash flow. The company's performance highlights that strong AI demand doesn't always translate into immediate stock gains if supply chain issues persist.

items.title: CN Reports August Grain Movement
items.summary: Canadian National Railway Company (CN) announced a new monthly record for grain movement in August, transporting 2.50 million metric tonnes (MMT) from Western Canada, surpassing the previous record set in August 2020. This performance marks a strong start to the 2026–27 crop year, attributed to strong customer demand, collaboration with supply chain partners, and effective operational execution. CN plans to maintain this momentum through the fall harvest, ensuring reliable service for its partners.

items.title: Exxon’s Dividend Looks Safe Today—But What If Oil Prices Tumble?
items.summary: Exxon Mobil recently raised its dividend to $1.03 per share quarterly, extending a 43-year growth streak, even as crude oil prices briefly dropped below $58 a barrel in late 2025. CEO Darren Woods projects Exxon's free cash flow will double by 2030, driven by $16.3 billion in cost savings and profits from Guyana operations. Despite a 2.55% dividend yield, the company's strong coverage, recent share buyback plan, and significant year-to-date stock surge offer investors confidence in its financial durability against potential oil price declines.

items.title: Making Sense of Indonesia’s Doom Loop: Opportunity Amid Uncertainty
items.summary: Indonesia, under President Prabowo, presents a complex investment landscape characterized by both economic challenges like a plummeting rupiah and positive indicators such as projected GDP growth and increased foreign direct investment. The administration's centralized power allows swift policy enactment focused on economic nationalism, but a lack of consistent communication and frequent policy shifts create regulatory uncertainty. Despite these risks, Indonesia remains an attractive long-term growth market, requiring investors to adapt by focusing on continuous intelligence, robust stakeholder engagement, and comprehensive risk management.

items.title: PPL named one of nation’s top utilities for economic development
items.summary: PPL Electric Utilities has been recognized by Site Selection magazine as one of the nation's Top Utilities in Economic Development. This award highlights PPL's efforts in attracting jobs, investment, and opportunities to its service territory in Eastern and Central Pennsylvania, working collaboratively with businesses, communities, and economic development partners. In 2025, PPL Electric supported 20 projects, resulting in over $12.8 billion in capital investment and 1,775 new jobs across various sectors.

items.title: Steelworkers remain working under contract extensions
items.summary: Thousands of steelworkers in northeastern Minnesota continue to work under extended labor contracts as negotiations between the United Steelworkers (USW) union, Cleveland-Cliffs Inc., and United States Steel Corp. are ongoing. The previous contracts expired on September 1, and negotiations have been extended for 30 days. Key issues include healthcare, pensions, safety, wages, paid time off, and retiree healthcare.
